purpose: Does model complexity add predictive or economic value when simple models receive exactly the same information as MTST? Model family is the only thing that varies.

information_parity.flatten_order: column j = timestep t * n_features + feature f, t oldest first
information_parity.sample_construction: nn.dataset.build_windows, reached through nn.train.prepare_research_windows (train and inner validation) and nn.train.score_frozen_split (outer validation) — the same calls nn.walkforward makes for MTST
information_parity.scaling: nn.dataset.StandardScaler fitted on the fold's training rows only and applied unchanged to inner and outer validation, exactly as for MTST. The tree models do not require scaling — a positive per-feature affine map cannot change which rows fall on which side of a split — but they are given the same scaled array so that no model in this benchmark sees a different number from the one MTST saw

buy_and_hold.description: buy at the close of the first scored candle, hold, sell at the close of the candle that closes the last scored sample's label horizon
buy_and_hold.window: continuous market span (not the scored-sample set)
buy_and_hold.cost_model: one round trip charged once over the whole hold
buy_and_hold.per_trade_sharpe_reason: undefined: a single trade has no dispersion to measure
buy_and_hold.annualised_sharpe_reason: unavailable: the hold spans 85 calendar interval(s) absent from the processed dataset. What price did in between is not recorded there, so a candle-level series comparable to the strategy's cannot be built without inventing a path
